paragraphs: Predicting a road accident requires distinguishing an approaching collision from ordinary driving. Many existing systems assign a risk score to each video frame, but train with labels that mark every frame in an accident video as positive. That supervision blurs the difference between an uneventful early moment and the seconds immediately preceding a crash.

This paper instead predicts accident scores at several future times, such as 0.1 to 2.0 seconds ahead. Precisely annotated collision times provide the training signal. A snippet encoder captures motion and spatial relationships across a short video segment, while a Transformer decoder uses separate temporal queries to produce predictions for all future horizons together.

The evaluation also makes false alarms central: warning lead time and recall are reported only when the false alarm rate stays within an acceptable range. Experiments report better recall and earlier anticipation under those constraints. The contribution therefore links a more precise prediction target with an evaluation that rewards useful warnings without overlooking excessive alerts.
neurips-2025-accident-anticipation-via-t.tldr: Predicting when a collision may occur improves accident anticipation under evaluation constraints that explicitly limit false alarms.

paragraphs: AI-Researcher brings multiple stages of scientific work into an autonomous system. Its scope runs from reviewing literature and proposing hypotheses through implementing algorithms and preparing a publication-ready manuscript. The intended contribution is coordination across the research process, using language models' reasoning and coding capabilities with minimal human intervention.

To evaluate that broader capability, the authors introduce Scientist-Bench. It draws on research papers across different AI domains and includes both guided innovation and open-ended exploration. These two task types examine research under different levels of direction, making the benchmark relevant to more than simply implementing an already specified algorithm.

The experiments report strong implementation success and generated papers approaching human-level quality. These are findings from the authors' evaluation of the system, rather than a claim that every aspect of scientific judgment has been automated. The work presents autonomous research as a possible complement to human researchers, with coordinated systems exploring candidate solutions across an extended workflow.
neurips-2025-ai-researcher-autonomous-sc.tldr: AI-Researcher coordinates an autonomous research workflow and introduces a benchmark for evaluating guided and open-ended scientific work.

paragraphs: Audio-language models face jailbreak attempts that exploit the audio modality itself. The paper describes defenses transferred from text jailbreaks or traditional audio attacks as largely ineffective against these threats. ALMGuard addresses this mismatch with a defense designed specifically for models that jointly process audio and language.

Its central assumption is that these models already contain shortcuts associated with safety-aligned behavior. The method searches for reusable audio perturbations that trigger those shortcuts during inference. To preserve ordinary speech understanding, a Mel-Gradient Sparse Mask confines changes to frequency bins that are sensitive to jailbreaks but comparatively insensitive to speech understanding. This makes the choice of where to perturb part of the defense.

The authors provide theoretical analysis and experiments supporting robustness against both previously seen and unseen attacks. Across four models, they report an average attack success rate of 4.6% for advanced audio-language jailbreaks while retaining comparable performance on benign benchmarks. The findings support activating existing safety behavior through carefully targeted input changes, conditional on the framework's shortcut assumption.
neurips-2025-almguard-safety-shortcuts-a.tldr: ALMGuard uses targeted audio perturbations to activate assumed safety shortcuts while preserving performance on benign tasks.

paragraphs: Two-dimensional Gaussian splatting represents scenes in a way that supports consistent views and accurate surface geometry. However, changing the camera zoom or field of view can introduce severe rendering artifacts when the sampling rate differs from training. The paper attributes this problem to unconstrained representation frequencies and an ineffective screen-space clamping method.

AA-2DGS addresses the representation first. A flat smoothing kernel in world space limits the frequency content of each Gaussian primitive according to the highest sampling frequency available in the training views. This connects the detail stored in the representation to the observations that support it, and the authors report that it eliminates high-frequency artifacts when zooming in.

The second component handles filtering in each splat's local object space. An affine approximation to the mapping between rays and splat intersections makes a Mip filter efficient to apply there. Together, these changes are presented as improving rendering across scales while retaining the geometric benefits of 2DGS. The contribution directly targets how scene detail behaves when viewing conditions change.
neurips-2025-anti-aliased-2d-gaussian-sp.tldr: AA-2DGS combines frequency constraints and local splat filtering to improve rendering when camera scale changes.

paragraphs: Off-policy reinforcement learning offers attractive simplicity and data efficiency for aligning language models, but its performance can lag behind on-policy methods. This paper studies how the balance between encouraging good outputs and discouraging bad ones affects that tradeoff. It focuses on a simple REINFORCE update with an adjustable reward baseline.

The update uses an advantage equal to reward minus the baseline. Adjusting that baseline changes which samples receive positive or negative signals and how strongly they contribute. The authors prove a policy improvement guarantee when the baseline is a lower bound on expected reward. That condition is central: the guarantee does not apply to an arbitrary baseline choice.

Their analysis indicates that off-policy updates benefit from placing more emphasis on positive rewards than on negative ones, whereas on-policy updates can safely use both signals. Experiments in a controlled stochastic bandit setting and language-model reasoning fine-tuning support this finding. The practical implication is that reward asymmetry can be a principled design choice when learning from off-policy data.
neurips-2025-asymmetric-reinforce-for-of.tldr: A conditional policy improvement guarantee and experiments support emphasizing positive rewards in off-policy REINFORCE updates.

paragraphs: Border basis algorithms are tools for working with polynomial equation systems, particularly those with finitely many solutions. Their computational cost can be high, while learned alternatives may sacrifice correctness. This paper integrates a Transformer into the traditional computation while retaining guarantees about the final algebraic result.

The learned component serves as an oracle that identifies expensive reduction steps that can be eliminated. The authors find that these steps dominate runtime, so selectively consulting the oracle during critical phases targets a major source of cost. The resulting Oracle Border Basis Algorithm achieves speedups of up to 3.5 times over the base algorithm without compromising output correctness.

The work also develops the machinery needed to train that oracle. It supplies a sampling method and a sampling theorem for border bases, together with a representation organized around monomials. This encoding reduces the tokens needed for an n-variable polynomial by a factor of O(n). These contributions make learned guidance more practical inside a symbolic algorithm whose correctness guarantees remain intact.
neurips-2025-computational-algebra-with-.tldr: A Transformer oracle accelerates border basis computation by removing expensive reduction steps while preserving output correctness.

paragraphs: A visual dataset can associate a class with recurring backgrounds, textures, or accompanying objects. Finding these patterns usually requires detailed annotations that are expensive to obtain. ConceptScope automates part of this auditing process by discovering interpretable visual concepts from representations produced by vision foundation models.

Sparse autoencoders extract concepts, which the framework then categorizes as target, context, or bias according to their semantic relevance and statistical relationship with class labels. This supports descriptions of individual classes and the construction of concept-based subgroups for robustness evaluation. Concept activations also indicate image regions, connecting a detected pattern to visible evidence within an image.

Comparisons with annotated datasets show coverage of concepts ranging from objects and backgrounds to facial attributes, emotions, and actions. The authors report spatial attributions that align with meaningful regions, detection of known background bias in Waterbirds, and discovery of previously unannotated co-occurring objects in ImageNet. These results position ConceptScope as a practical tool for identifying dataset patterns that warrant closer model diagnosis.
neurips-2025-conceptscope-characterizing.tldr: ConceptScope discovers interpretable visual concepts to characterize datasets, detect biases, and organize robustness evaluations.

paragraphs: Choosing a small training subset can reduce the cost of teaching multimodal models to follow visual instructions. However, the authors observe that both full-dataset training and existing selection methods can carry dataset biases into model behavior. Examples include reliance on position and correlations that do not reflect the intended task.

ARDS selects data with those weaknesses in mind. It first applies task-specific changes to visual and textual inputs to identify evaluation subgroups where performance is worst. It then prioritizes training samples that are semantically close to those subgroups in a multimodal embedding space. This connects selection to observed vulnerabilities without requiring downstream data access or expensive gradient calculations.

Experiments report improvements in both robustness and data efficiency. The authors also show that mixtures selected using a smaller model transfer effectively to larger architectures. That result matters because the selection effort can remain useful beyond the model that produced it. The paper's central finding is that the composition of a compact training set can address weaknesses that simply using more data does not resolve.
neurips-2025-data-selection-matters-towa.tldr: ARDS selects visual instruction data around observed weaknesses, improving robustness and data efficiency across tested models.

paragraphs: Estimating actual distances from a single image can be difficult because visual appearance may leave scale ambiguous or create misleading depth cues. Traditional methods that infer depth by changing focus face a different constraint: low acquisition sampling rates. This paper combines event-based focus information with image foundation models to improve dense metric depth estimation.

The method gathers events triggered while focus is swept and organizes them into Event-based Differential Focus Volumes. These volumes are converted into sparse maps of metric depth. An Event-based Depth Prompting Network then uses those maps to guide dense depth prediction. The sparse measurements supply distance information, while the prompted model produces a depth estimate across the image.

The authors also construct synthetic and real-captured datasets for training and comparing frame-based and event-based approaches. Their quantitative and qualitative evaluations report superior performance over existing methods in both in-domain and zero-shot experiments. The contribution is a way to connect focus-derived metric information with the dense prediction abilities of image models through prompting.
neurips-2025-dense-metric-depth-estimati.tldr: Event measurements collected during focus sweeping provide sparse metric depth prompts that improve dense depth prediction.

paragraphs: A policy trained with a simulator may encounter different conditions in practice. This paper studies decision-making that maximizes reward while satisfying constraints against the worst stochastic model within an uncertainty set. The set is centered around an unknown nominal model, so robustness is defined relative to that specified range of uncertainty.

Standard constrained optimization tools encounter two obstacles here. Strong duality is absent, undermining the usual primal-dual approach, and the worst model for reward may differ from the worst model for constraints. The proposed method responds by prioritizing reduction of the constraint value when constraints are unsatisfied, then maximizing robust reward when they are satisfied.

The authors prove that the algorithm finds a feasible policy with at most epsilon suboptimality after O(epsilon^-2) iterations. It also avoids the binary search used by the compared state-of-the-art method. The paper reports reduced computation time and better performance, especially for continuous state spaces. Its contribution combines a direct optimization strategy with a quantitative guarantee on the iterations needed to reach the stated objective.
neurips-2025-efficient-policy-optimizati.tldr: Alternating between constraint satisfaction and robust reward optimization yields a feasible, near-optimal policy with an iteration guarantee.

paragraphs: Faces and people appear throughout everyday images, making their interpretation an important capability for multimodal assistants. Face-Human-Bench addresses the lack of a comprehensive evaluation focused on this area. The paper begins with a three-level hierarchy of abilities, giving the benchmark an explicit structure for organizing what models are asked to understand.

The authors draw images and annotations from publicly available face and human datasets. A semi-automatic pipeline turns those materials into benchmark problems. The resulting development and test sets each contain 1,800 problems, with support for both English and Chinese. This provides a common evaluation resource across models and the two supported languages.

The study evaluates 25 multimodal language models and examines relationships between abilities, sensitivity to targets' relative positions, and the effects of chain-of-thought prompting. It also investigates which abilities could benefit from specialist models. The abstract describes these evaluation questions without reporting a particular ranking or directional outcome. The contribution is a structured benchmark and analysis of distinct dimensions of face and human understanding.
neurips-2025-face-human-bench-a-comprehe.tldr: Face-Human-Bench organizes and evaluates multimodal assistants' face and human understanding through a bilingual, structured benchmark.

paragraphs: When options have several reward dimensions, identifying the best choices requires a rule for comparing tradeoffs. This paper studies finding the Pareto-optimal set with a specified confidence level, using a given preference cone to order reward vectors. The challenge is to use observations efficiently while keeping the calculations that guide sampling tractable.

FraPPE addresses an optimization problem embedded in the existing sample-complexity lower bound. The authors derive three structural properties that simplify its minimization component, then use a Frank-Wolfe optimizer for the maximization component. Together, these steps solve the max-min problem in O(KL²) time for K options and L reward dimensions, including arbitrary preference cones.

The paper proves that FraPPE attains optimal sample complexity asymptotically. That is a limiting guarantee, rather than a claim of exact optimality for every finite experiment. Numerical tests on synthetic and real datasets report the lowest sample requirements among the compared algorithms for recovering the exact Pareto set. The result combines efficient computation with a theoretically optimal sampling objective.
neurips-2025-frappe-fast-and-efficient-p.tldr: FraPPE makes preference-based Pareto-set exploration computationally efficient while attaining asymptotically optimal sample complexity.

paragraphs: Point cloud registration aligns different collections of 3D points describing a scene. Geometry alone can become unreliable when scans are incomplete or share very little overlap. GeGS-PCR combines geometric structure, color, and Gaussian information in a two-stage approach intended to make those difficult alignments more robust.

A dedicated color encoder extracts information at multiple levels, while a Geometric-3DGS module represents neighborhoods around colored superpoints to provide an invariant geometric-color context. The method also uses LORA optimization and fast differentiable rendering to refine registration. A joint photometric loss brings geometric and color information into the optimization, supporting alignment when shared point coverage is extremely limited.

The evaluation includes a colorized Kitti dataset called ColorKitti, alongside Color3DMatch and Color3DLoMatch. The authors report registration recall reaching 99.9%, relative rotation error as low as 0.013, and relative translation error as low as 0.024, with at least a twofold precision improvement. These results support combining appearance and geometry within registration, including the challenging overlap conditions investigated in the paper.
neurips-2025-gegs-pcr-fast-and-robust-co.tldr: GeGS-PCR combines color, geometry, and Gaussian representations to improve point cloud alignment under low overlap and incomplete observations.

paragraphs: Understanding why gradient-based training performs well on unseen data remains a theoretical challenge. This paper studies gradient flow and develops a generalization bound that incorporates the full training trajectory. Its central object is a data-dependent loss path kernel, which reflects both the dataset and the dynamics of optimization.

The bound has a form aligned with classical kernel-method guarantees involving a function norm and a kernel trace. Unlike a static kernel, the loss path kernel follows the evolving training process. The result also highlights the role of training-loss gradient norms along that path. The proof combines stability analysis with uniform convergence arguments based on Rademacher complexity.

The authors show that their result recovers existing kernel regression bounds for overparameterized neural networks and captures neural networks' feature-learning capability relative to kernel methods. Experiments on real-world datasets find that the bounds correlate well with the measured generalization gap. This empirical agreement supports the usefulness of tracking optimization history when assessing generalization, alongside the formal guarantee itself.
neurips-2025-generalization-bound-of-gra.tldr: A loss path kernel incorporates the training trajectory into a generalization bound for gradient flow.

paragraphs: Generating longer reasoning sequences or more parallel attempts can improve language-model accuracy, but it increases inference cost. This paper identifies the Transformer key-value cache as the relevant bottleneck and asks whether compressing it can fund more generation within the same compute budget. The benefit depends on preserving accuracy at substantial compression levels.

Dynamic Memory Sparsification makes this tradeoff more practical by learning to sparsify the cache in 1,000 training steps, reaching eightfold compression. It delays eviction of cached tokens, allowing representations to merge implicitly before information is discarded. The authors report better accuracy than training-free sparse attention at this compression setting.

Across multiple model families, the resulting inference-time hyper-scaling improves accuracy at comparable latency and memory load. For Qwen-R1 32B, the reported gains are 9.1 points on AIME 24, 7.6 on GPQA, and 9.6 on LiveCodeBench for equivalent memory reads on average. The findings show how cache efficiency can be reinvested in reasoning, provided compression retains the information needed for accurate generation.
neurips-2025-inference-time-hyper-scalin.tldr: Learned KV-cache compression enables more inference-time reasoning and improves tested accuracy at comparable resource costs.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning a language model on medical material can add knowledge while eroding what the model already knows. This paper identifies a specific pattern: prior knowledge that is semantically or topically close to the new content is more likely to be forgotten. Unrelated knowledge shows comparatively little degradation in the authors' investigation.

InternAL uses that observation to decide which existing knowledge should accompany the new training material. It derives questions from the knowledge being injected and prompts the model to reveal related internal knowledge. Those responses augment the injection dataset, giving training an explicit opportunity to retain nearby prior knowledge while learning the new content.

Experiments with LLaMA and Qwen models show significant reductions in proximity-related forgetting while maintaining strong knowledge injection performance. The authors also report that existing mitigation techniques do not effectively address this particular pattern. The findings motivate a targeted approach to retention: use the relationship between old and new knowledge to select what should be revisited during domain adaptation.
neurips-2025-investigating-and-mitigatin.tldr: InternAL revisits a model's related prior knowledge during medical fine-tuning to reduce proximity-dependent forgetting.

paragraphs: An influence function describes how a statistical quantity changes as its underlying probability distribution is perturbed. It is important for optimizing over distributions, constructing efficient estimators, and carrying out statistical inference. Obtaining it often requires a difficult analytical derivation, which can obstruct the use of those methods.

This paper develops a spectral representation that makes influence-function estimation more automatic. The method uses kernel principal component analysis to identify components and then calculates numerical pathwise derivatives along them. These ingredients produce a low-rank estimator in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, allowing the calculation to proceed without a user-supplied analytical influence function.

The authors derive the representation and prove consistency of the proposed estimator. The contribution therefore includes both a computational construction and a theoretical justification for its convergence. Its practical significance lies in turning an otherwise manual derivation into a procedure built around kernel components and numerical derivatives, while preserving a formal connection to the influence function being estimated.
neurips-2025-kernel-von-mises-formula-of.tldr: A kernel spectral representation enables influence-function estimation without manual analytical derivation and comes with a consistency proof.

paragraphs: LMFusion adds image understanding and generation to an existing text language model, enabling text and images to appear in arbitrary sequences. It reuses Llama-3's weights for autoregressive text processing and adds parallel Transformer modules that process images through diffusion. This makes pretrained language capability a foundation for multimodal development.

Each modality has its own feedforward layers, attention projections, and normalization layers. Shared self-attention permits interaction between text and image features, while the text-specific modules remain frozen during training. Only the image-specific modules are trained. The architecture therefore combines cross-modal communication with separate pathways for developing visual capabilities and retaining the existing language system.

Compared with methods trained from scratch for multimodal generation, experiments report 20% better image understanding and 3.6% better image generation using half the FLOPs, while maintaining Llama-3's language capabilities. The authors also adapt existing vision-language models for generation. These results support reusing prior training investment and developing language and vision components in parallel within a shared multimodal framework.
neurips-2025-lmfusion-adapting-pretraine.tldr: LMFusion adds trainable image modules to pretrained language models, enabling multimodal generation while retaining language capabilities.

paragraphs: Virtual try-on must make clothing fit a person's pose while preserving fabric textures and other fine details. PhysDiff-VTON addresses both demands within a diffusion-based image-generation framework. Its design introduces physics-inspired mechanisms into garment deformation and the sequence of denoising steps used to create the final image.

A pose-guided warping module predicts spatial offsets from human pose information to simulate fabric dynamics. A separate wavelet-based decomposition supports attention to different frequency content, helping preserve detailed textures. The sampling strategy then optimizes the denoising trajectory using least-action principles, enforcing coherence across that trajectory, spatial smoothness, and structural consistency at multiple scales.

Evaluations across multiple datasets report significant gains in geometric plausibility and perceptual quality compared with existing approaches. These findings connect the framework's two concerns: plausible garment shape and faithful appearance. The physics-inspired treatment guides both how clothing features move and how the image is progressively generated, supporting more realistic try-on images without treating fine garment detail as a separate finishing step.
neurips-2025-physdiff-vton-cross-domain-.tldr: PhysDiff-VTON combines pose-guided deformation, frequency-aware detail preservation, and physics-inspired diffusion sampling for more plausible virtual try-on.

paragraphs: Many recurrent architectures process information as a sequence, forcing images or graphs into a predetermined order. This paper extends linear recurrence to multidimensional structures through pLSTMs. The architecture operates on directed acyclic graphs, allowing the organization of the data to participate directly in how information is propagated.

Source, Transition, and Mark gates act on the graph's linegraph and enable parallel computation analogous to scans and chunkwise recurrence in sequential models. For one- and two-dimensional regular grids, the scheme has an efficient logarithmic-time implementation. Two operating modes address vanishing or exploding activations and gradients over long graph distances: one emphasizes directed propagation, while the other distributes information diffusively.

The authors introduce a synthetic arrow-pointing task that requires long-distance directional information. In those experiments, pLSTMs generalize well to larger images while Transformers struggle to extrapolate. They also report strong results on established molecular graph and vision benchmarks. The findings support structured recurrence as a useful approach to long-range information processing beyond ordinary sequences.
neurips-2025-plstm-parallelizable-linear.tldr: pLSTMs extend parallelizable linear recurrence to directed acyclic graphs and demonstrate strong long-distance reasoning on structured data.

paragraphs: This paper establishes theoretical limits for one-layer softmax Transformers on three reasoning tasks. These include examining token triplets, composing functions, and composing binary relations. The analysis allows arbitrarily many precision bits, even infinite precision, so the demonstrated limits cannot be attributed simply to insufficient numerical precision.

The authors introduce Strassen attention and prove that a one-layer Transformer equipped with it can, in principle, solve all three tasks. The mechanism also has sub-cubic running time, improving scalability relative to similar higher-order attention mechanisms. This connects an expressivity result to a computational consideration: the proposed capability does not require the cubic scaling associated with those alternatives.

Experiments compare Strassen attention with standard, higher-order, and triangular attention. Strassen attention significantly outperforms standard attention on all the studied tasks, while the comparisons help distinguish the mechanisms' strengths and limitations. The theoretical statements concern the specified one-layer setting, and the constructive result establishes possible solvability. Together, the proofs and experiments motivate attention design as a route to improving compositional reasoning.
neurips-2025-strassen-attention-split-vc.tldr: Strassen attention lets one-layer Transformers theoretically solve three tasks that defeat one-layer softmax attention, with sub-cubic runtime.

paragraphs: In constrained decision-making, a learner seeks high reward while limiting constraint violations. When rewards and constraints are fully adversarial, a known impossibility result rules out simultaneously sublinear regret and violation against a best-in-hindsight policy satisfying constraints on average. This paper studies intermediate environments where the amount of adversarial variation can be quantified.

The proposed algorithms achieve regret and positive constraint violation bounded by roughly sqrt(T) + C, up to logarithmic factors, under bandit feedback. Here, T is the interaction horizon and C measures the adverseness of rewards and constraints. The guarantee degrades smoothly with C, linking relatively stable environments to more hostile ones within the same analysis.

The authors first provide an algorithm that knows C, then remove that requirement through a procedure that selects among multiple algorithm instances while balancing reward regret and constraint violation. In the worst case C grows proportionally to T, so the result remains consistent with the original impossibility theorem. The advance is an adaptive guarantee for less adverse settings, rather than a universal escape from that barrier.
neurips-2025-taming-adversarial-constrai.tldr: The proposed constrained-learning algorithms achieve guarantees that degrade smoothly with environmental adverseness, even when its level is unknown.

paragraphs: Improving a language model's reasoning commonly involves labeled training examples or costly generation of candidate solutions. This paper investigates a much smaller training signal: the opening tokens of reasoning traces. Its motivation is prefix self-consistency, the observation that different solution trajectories often share their initial reasoning steps.

Unsupervised Prefix Fine-Tuning trains only on these initial substrings, sometimes using as few as eight tokens. This removes the need for labeled data or exhaustive sampling in the proposed method. Additional analysis finds that errors tend to occur later in reasoning and that training on prefixes preserves the model's structural knowledge, supporting the choice to concentrate on the opening steps.

On reasoning benchmarks, UPFT matches supervised approaches such as Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning while reducing training time by 75% and sampling cost by 99%. These are empirical findings from the reported comparisons. They suggest that a very limited, unsupervised portion of generated reasoning can provide a useful adaptation signal without requiring training on complete solution trajectories.
neurips-2025-the-first-few-tokens-are-al.tldr: Fine-tuning on short reasoning prefixes matches supervised methods in reported experiments while sharply reducing training and sampling costs.

paragraphs: TheAgentCompany evaluates whether language-model agents can perform professional tasks through ordinary computer interactions. It creates a self-contained environment resembling a small software company, including internal websites and data. Agents work by browsing, writing code, running programs, and communicating with coworkers, bringing several kinds of digital activity into one benchmark.

The benchmark is extensible and contains varied tasks representative of work in that setting. The authors test agents powered by both closed API-based models and open-weight models. This setup examines whether an agent can complete workplace tasks autonomously within a shared simulated environment, rather than assessing only an isolated language-model response.

The strongest tested agent completes 30% of tasks autonomously. The authors find that a substantial portion of simpler tasks is achievable, while difficult tasks requiring sustained activity over a longer horizon remain beyond the tested systems. The result provides a qualified view of workplace automation: demonstrated task completion coexists with substantial limits on extended workflows, even inside an environment designed for systematic evaluation.
neurips-2025-theagentcompany-benchmarkin.tldr: In a simulated software workplace, the strongest tested agent completes 30% of tasks autonomously but struggles with difficult long-horizon work.

paragraphs: Different tables can describe related entities and attributes, making their information potentially useful in combination. Existing tabular learning methods can struggle to characterize and use this complementarity. This paper proposes a unified formulation for multi-table learning that addresses both measuring the relationship between tables and integrating their information.

The proposed complementarity strength metric combines relevance, similarity, and informativeness. It is intended to quantify how much complementary information exists across tables. The authors also formalize learning tasks and loss functions, giving the problem an explicit mathematical structure. Their ATCA-Net architecture uses adaptive table encoders and cross-table attention to integrate information from distinct tables simultaneously.

Experiments show that ATCA-Net makes effective use of complementary information and that the metric captures the richness of complementarity across multiple tables. These findings support the two parts of the proposal together: a measure of what tables contribute jointly and a network designed to use those contributions. The paper presents this combination as a foundation for more systematic multi-table learning.
neurips-2025-towards-multi-table-learnin.tldr: A complementarity metric and cross-table attention network provide a unified approach to measuring and combining information across tables.
